title: Authorization Logging, Audit Pipeline, and Deprovisioning Guidance
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines standardized guidance for: (1) producing high-fidelity authorization and access logs for all tenant-facing control planes and admin surfaces; (2) the audit log collection and query pipeline used for compliance evidence; and (3) a consistent account and role deprovisioning procedure that satisfies privacy, retention, and regulatory constraints. The intent is to reduce variance across teams, ensure defensible evidence for auditors, and lower risk from orphaned privileges.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference control planes and internal admin consoles (hosted API control plane, Dedicated control UI, Private control plane operator interfaces, Console service).
- Includes service-to-service auth events, human-initiated role changes, provisioning/deprovisioning, and API key lifecycle events.
- Excludes low-level infrastructure logs (hypervisor or host OS metrics) other than pointers where required for investigations.

Principles:
1) Immutable, timestamped events: Every authorization-related event must be emitted as an append-only record with RFC3339 timestamps and a stable event_id.
2) Context-rich records: Events must include subject (actor id), object (resource id), action, outcome (allowed/denied), request_context (ip, region, user_agent), and relevant policy_version.
3) Reliable transport & retention: Logs are transmitted to the centralized audit pipeline with at-least-once delivery semantics, signed/encrypted in transit, and retained per the retention matrix below.
4) Least privilege and timely revocation: Deprovisioning must complete within SLA windows defined per role sensitivity.

Roles and role mappings (summary):
- ROLE_ADMIN: Full control for account-level admin operations (create/delete-project, billing changes). Sensitive; deprovision SLA: 1 business hour.
- ROLE_DEPLOY: Can deploy and manage model serving configurations. Deprovision SLA: 4 business hours.
- ROLE_READONLY: Observability and billing read access. Deprovision SLA: 5 business days.
- SERVICE_PRINCIPAL: Machine principals with scoped permissions (e.g., model-scheduler). Rotation and deprovisioning handled via secrets-management automation.

Required event schema (example):
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp: 2026-02-12T14:23:05Z
- actor_id: user:alice@example.com | service:model-scheduler
- actor_type: human | service
- action: api_key.rotate | role.assign | role.revoke | auth.attempt
- resource_type: project | route | model | api_key
- resource_id: prj-12345
- outcome: allow | deny | error
- policy_version: v1.3
- region: us-west-2
- request_id: req-000123
- additional: {"ip":"3.80.4.5","user_agent":"CI/1.0"}

(Teams must ensure logs conform to this schema; sample JSON event is in Appendix A.)

Logging & audit pipeline (architecture):
- Emitters: control-plane services (auth, iam-service, api-gateway), management UI, onboarding lambdas, bastion and jump hosts (operator actions).
- Collector: local write-ahead queue -> secure forwarder (TLS+mutual-auth) -> central Kafka topic partitioned by tenant-region.
- Processing: stream enrichment jobs (policy_version attach, user directory merge) -> normalized audit index (Elasticsearch-like store) -> cold storage (encrypted object storage) for raw events.
- Access: audit UI (read-only) for auditors, and a secured query API for automated evidence assembly.

SLOs & alerting for the pipeline:
- Delivery latency: 99th percentile < 15s from event emit to central topic.
- Enrichment latency: median < 60s, 95th < 5m.
- Missing event threshold: Alert if >0.1% events fail forwarder for >5m.
- Retention policy enforcement: nightly job validates cold-storage immutability flags; alerts on divergence.

Data residency & retention matrix (high-level):
- Auth events (user role changes, login, API key events): 7 years for regulated enterprise customers by default, 2 years for standard customers.
- Service-to-service auth telemetry (non-identifying): 90 days hot, 2 years cold.
- For customers with local residency requirements, encrypted raw events must be stored in the requested geo and evidence pointers maintained centrally.

Deprovisioning procedure (operational run):
Objective: Revoke all entitlements for a subject (user or service) and capture an audit trail suitable for compliance and forensic review.
Steps:
1) Initiate: Ticket is opened in access-management queue (automated for offboarding triggers from HR/SCIM or manual for emergency).
2) Quarantine steps (if high-risk): Immediately revoke interactive sessions and suspend API keys. Create Timeboxed flag on account: suspended=true.
3) Role revocation: Sequentially revoke roles from highest privilege to lowest using iam-service API. Example command:
   curl -X POST https://iam.redwood.example/v1/roles/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' -d '{"actor_id":"user:bob@example.com","roles":["ROLE_ADMIN","ROLE_DEPLOY"]}'
4) Service principal handling: Rotate/seal secrets in secrets manager and replace credentials for dependent workflows.
5) Resource transfer: Reassign ownerable assets (projects, routes) per asset transfer checklist in Appendix B.
6) Finalize: Mark account deprovisioned in identity store and export full audit snapshot (raw events + normalized index entries) into evidence bucket.
7) Evidence packaging: Use the evidence API to create a signed package: evidence-api create --account prj-12345 --range "2025-01-01:2026-03-01" --format ndjson
8) Post-ops verification: Run the verification queries (see Appendix C) and confirm no privileged sessions remain.

Deprovisioning SLAs by sensitivity:
- High (admin, billing): 1 hour (business)
- Medium (deployment): 4 hours (business)
- Low (read-only): 5 business days

Evidence assembly for audits (recommended minimal set):
- Audit snapshot: All raw events for the subject in the requested window (ndjson), with integrity hashes and a signed manifest.
- IAM state: Time-series snapshot of role assignments and policy_versions.
- Secrets events: API key rotation/revoke events and secret-store rotation logs.
- Access paths: Console login sessions, bastion session recordings (if applicable), and SSO assertion logs.
- Artifact list: List of artifacts (configs, model versions) the subject had owner rights to at the time.

Exception & risk handling (authorization edge cases):
- Emergency elevation: Any emergency role escalation must be timebound, annotated with justification, and produce an immediate audit event. Post-facto review required within 24 hours.
- Delegation exceptions: Maintain an exception register with TTL. Exceptions must be approved by security and product.
- Risk scoring: Each pending exception is assigned a risk score (0-100) based on blast radius, sensitivity, and compensating controls. Scores >= 75 require exec sign-off.

Forensic checklist for incidents involving authz failures:
1) Freeze the central audit topic partition that contains the subject events.
2) Export raw events to isolated object storage with current access controls.
3) Record computed hashes and assert chain-of-custody with signatures.
4) Triage mapping: correlate with CI logs, deployment traces, and infra metrics.
5) Prepare evidence package for legal/compliance with redaction markers where PII is present.

Operational examples & snippets (Appendices):
- Appendix A: Sample JSON event (single-line ndjson) {"event_id":"111e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000","timestamp":"2026-02-12T14:23:05Z","actor_id":"user:alice@example.com","action":"role.revoke","resource_id":"prj-12345","outcome":"allow"} 

- Appendix B: Asset transfer checklist (table style in confluence):
  - Asset type | Owner field | Transfer action | Audit step
  - Project | project.owner | reassign -> iam-service.transferOwner() | record transfer event
  - Route | route.owner | set new owner | export route ACL snapshot

- Appendix C: Verification queries (Elasticsearch-like DSL):
  - Find recent admin revokes: {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"action":"role.revoke"}},{"term":{"resource_type":"project"}}],"filter":{"range":{"timestamp":{"gte":"now-7d"}}}}}}

Operational responsibilities and ownership:
- Emitters: Service teams (code owners) — ensure schema compliance and forwarder reliability.
- Collector & pipeline: infra/observability team — maintain SLOs, partitions, and enrichment jobs.
- Evidence packaging and legal handoffs: security & compliance team — create signed packages and manage auditor access.
- Deprovisioning execs: people-ops + security for HR-driven offboarding; product/platform for service principals.

Governance & review cadence:
- Quarterly tabletop exercises for deprovisioning incidents and emergency escalations.
- Monthly pipeline health report with retention verification metrics.
- Annual review of retention matrices and residency mappings with legal.

Appendix D: Change log
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft authored by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-02-10: Added deprovisioning SLAs and evidence packaging steps after review with infra team.
- 2026-03-01: Finalized retention matrix and added emergency elevation controls.

Contact: security@redwood.example for questions or to request a run of the evidence packaging job.
